newsitem.title: UK: Wilde reveals the self-importance of being Oscar.
newsitem.headline: Wilde reveals the self-importance of being Oscar.

text.p: Flamboyant playwright Oscar Wilde revealed the self-importance of being Oscar at an early age, a new literary discovery has revealed.
A previously unknown questionnaire filled in by Wilde at Oxford University in 1877 showed him honing his sarcastic wit at an early age.
Christie's the auctioneers told the London Times that the questionnaire will be auctioned next month.
Wilde, who died in penury after being disgraced and jailed for his homosexuality, mockingly told his fellow students that "reading my sonnets" was his favourite occupation.

The writer, who once told a U.S customs officer that all he had to declare was his genius, confessed in the questionnaire with great prescience that his aim in life was "success, fame or even notoriety."
